subject: Discovery recap and scheduling: 60-90m technical runthrough
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Monroe <alex@lumos.ai>, Priya Singh <priya@lumos.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-03-12T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap and scheduling: 60-90m technical runthrough

Thanks again for a productive discovery call this morning — really appreciated the openness on data flows and your performance targets. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Recap: Lumos is evaluating a hosted + private hybrid inference approach for your recommendation engine (high RPS, <120ms p95 target). Primary constraints: on-prem data residency, peak burst traffic, and budget guardrails.
- Goal for next session: 60–90 minute technical runthrough focused on architecture, integration touchpoints, and perf/cost sizing (we will bring an infra/serving engineer).

Proposed windows (all PST):
- Tue Apr 2: 09:00–10:30 or 14:00–15:30
- Wed Apr 3: 10:00–11:30 (preferred on our side)

Please let us know which slot works and who from Lumos should attend (ideally your ML lead + infra/engineer + procurement/PM if they have questions).

Prep from our side: Ben (SE) will demo a short model-serving prototype and Mina (Solutions Architect) will walk through network/KMS patterns for private deployments. I attached a short runthrough outline and a mutual action plan draft — feel free to add items.

Pre-call asks from you (helps us tailor the runthrough):
- example prompt/queries or synthetic load shape (tokens per request, QPS peaks)
- any strict compliance controls (retention windows, audit frequency)
- if you want cost-focused scenarios (e.g., reserved vs burst), say so and we'll include numbers

Thanks — happy to lock once you confirm attendees and one of the windows above.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0132

Attachments: redwood-runthrough-outline.pdf (1 page), mutual-action-plan-lumos.xlsx (stub)

From: Alex Monroe <alex@lumos.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-03-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap and scheduling: 60-90m technical runthrough

Tessa — thanks for the clear recap. Wed Apr 3 10:00–11:30 PST works best for us. I will invite Priya Singh (Head of ML) and Samir Patel (VP Eng).

A couple quick notes so Ben/Mina can prep effectively:
- We typically see bursts to ~150 QPS for recommendation endpoints; median request size is ~600 tokens after encoding.
- Our retention policy for model inputs is 30 days; we will need to confirm audit export formatting for SOC-type requests.
- We are particularly interested in a comparison of hosted vs dedicated reserved capacity from a cost-per-1M-token perspective.

If you can send the runthrough outline and any perf targets you use for benchmarks, that will help Priya prep the team. See you Apr 3 — calendar invite incoming from me.

— Alex
Alex Monroe
Head of Product
Lumos Analytics
alex@lumos.ai

Perfect — thanks Alex and looking forward to the invite. Locked: Wed Apr 3, 10:00–11:30 PST. I accepted the calendar hold and updated the invite to include Ben and Mina.

Proposed 75-minute agenda (we can extend to 90 if you want extra Q&A):
1) 10:00–10:10 — quick intros & recap of objectives (Tessa + Alex)
2) 10:10–10:35 — architecture & integration patterns (Mina)
3) 10:35–11:00 — demo: serving runtime, KV/prefix caching, and burst handling (Ben)
4) 11:00–11:15 — perf/cost scenarios and reserved vs burst economics (Ben + Mina)
5) 11:15–11:25 — compliance & private deployment checklist (Mina)
6) 11:25–11:30 — wrap, action items, next steps

Pre-call checklist for Lumos to send before Apr 1 if possible:
- short sample of request size or synthetic load profile (CSV ok)
- list of attendees with roles
- any non-negotiable compliance or audit artifacts (e.g., schema for audit export)

Ben and I will prepare two short slides showing p95 targets and a lightweight cost table for reserved vs burst usage. Attaching the runthrough outline and MAP again.

If you want to include anything else (e.g., procurement or legal early), flag that and we'll pull appropriate folks.

Cheers,
Tessa

Hi all — joining as the SE on Apr 3 and I’ll lead the demo portion. A few practical items from my side: 

- Can Priya/Samir drop a representative JSON of a typical request (headers + payload shape) or a short synthetic script we can run locally? That will let me reproduce realistic tokenization and show p95 numbers under a similar shape.
- For cost scenarios: do you have a target monthly token volume or a quarterly forecast we should model? even rough ranges are fine.
- If you have any internal network constraints (eg: only specific egress IPs allowed), please add them to the MAP so Mina can call that out.

I attached the one-page runthrough outline we mentioned; I’ll have a tiny demo notebook and a perf slide ready. Looking forward to it.

Thanks — Ben
